diagnostic_evidence.quote: We study nonlinear elliptic problems in variational form. Let $f \in V^*$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper fixes $f\in V^*=H^{-1}(\Omega)$ in Section 2 and never strengthens this. Yet the whole (C1) machinery is built on elementwise $L^2$ quantities: the element residual $\mathcal R_T(\sigma_h)=c(x,\tilde u_h)-f-\nabla\!\cdot\sigma_h$ is measured in $\|\cdot\|_{L^2(T)}$ in \eqref{eq:eta_osc}, and the Marini reconstruction of Section 5 consumes $s_h=c(\cdot,\tilde u_h)-f$ through the $L^1$-projection $r_h=\Pi_T^0(s_h)$. For a general $f\in H^{-1}(\Omega)$ these objects are undefined, so the bound $\|\mathcal F(\tilde u_h)\|_{V^*}\le\eta(\sigma_h)$ of Theorem 4.3 and the explicit flux route of Section 5 are not well posed under the paper's stated hypotheses; the missing premise is never stated (Assumption 4.4 constrains only the diffusion coefficient).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard local hypothesis that $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ (so that $s_h\in L^2$ elementwise, $\mathcal R_T\in L^2(T)$ and $r_h=\Pi^0_T(s_h)$ are defined); no other change is needed anywhere in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised computable certificate for ingredient (C1) is unavailable for general data $f\in H^{-1}(\Omega)$: Theorem 4.3 (its weighted-Cauchy-Schwarz/oscillation proof) and the Marini reconstruction (Lemmas 5.1-5.2, which need $\Pi^0_T(s_h)$) are ill-posed as stated. The abstract NK theorem is conditional and unaffected, and the numerical section uses a smooth $f$.
issues.title: Certified residual bound (C1) is ill-defined because f is only assumed in V* = H^{-1}
issues.why_classification: Adding one standard local integrability condition on the data restores every statement, construction, rate and advertised guarantee; the method, conclusions and numerical results are unchanged and no new lemma or argument is needed.

Therefore, the $u$-dependent diffusion model \eqref{eq:quasi-u-diffusion} satisfies (C3) on $B_{\rho}$.
The key point is that the dependence of the principal diffusion coefficient on $u$ forces an $L^\infty$ control (here encoded in $C_\infty$).

issues.failure_explanation: Section 7.4 claims to deliver a computable Lipschitz function $L(\rho)$ in (7.20) for the quasilinear prototype $-\nabla\!\cdot(a(x,u)\nabla u)=f$, thereby satisfying (C3) on $B_\rho$. Both derivations (the $L^\infty$ coefficient-difference bounds (7.17) and the second-term estimate (7.19)) consume the assumed ingredients $\|v\|_{L^\infty}\le C_\infty\|v\|_V$ for all $v\in V$ and $\|w\|_{L^\infty}\le M_\infty(\rho)$ for all $w\in B_\rho$. Both are false in the paper's own setting: with $V=H^1_0(\Omega)$ and $d\in\{2,3\}$, $H^1_0$ does not embed into $L^\infty$ (the paper itself invokes only $p\in[2,\infty)$ for $d=2$ and $p\in[2,6]$ for $d=3$), and consequently $\sup_{w\in B_\rho}\|w\|_{L^\infty}=\infty$ for every $\rho>0$, so finite computable $C_\infty$, $M_\infty(\rho)$, $K_1(\rho)$, $K_2(\rho)$ covering all states of the ball do not exist. The derivation is therefore vacuous and establishes none of the advertised Lipschitz ingredient for the quasilinear model.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claim explicitly: present the computation as conditional on an a priori $L^\infty$ control that the paper does not (and cannot) certify for $V$-balls in $d\ge2$, or restrict the illustration to $d=1$ (where $H^1_0\hookrightarrow L^\infty$ holds); state that no computable (C3) bound is provided for $u$-dependent diffusion in $d\ge2$.
issues.overall_effect: The only instantiation of ingredient (C3) for quasilinear, $u$-dependent diffusion is unsupported, so the advertised workflow cannot be run for that model class in $d\ge2$; the semilinear route (Lemma 7.1, Examples 7.3-7.4), the abstract NK theorem and the numerical guarantees are unaffected.
issues.title: Quasilinear (C3) example assumes a nonexistent L-infinity control on the energy-norm ball
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained weakening of one auxiliary example (or a restriction to $d=1$), not new proof architecture, and the paper's central workflow, rates and numerical guarantees survive; but the loss is real because the only advertised (C3) route for $u$-dependent diffusion is abandoned, which exceeds a minor local fix.
